# Preface {.unnumbered .unlisted}

<div style="display:flex">
<div style="flex:70%;margin-right:1em;">

This tutorial is intended for people with no prior experience with Git. The aim of the tutorial is to teach you how to use Git but also to understand how Git works, at least at a superficial level, so that you don't end up in the situation illustrated in the webcomic. To further reduce the risk of this scenario, we will learn how to use Git from the terminal, instead of using a GUI or a Git integration in a code editor. GUIs and Git integrations can make learning Git a less daunting endeavour, but they also come with the risk of using Git without developing a proper understanding of how it works. Furthermore, you can use Git from the terminal on any computer, whereas you might not have access to your favourite GUI or code editor on other systems that you need to use.

The tutorial is structured in two parts. Part I introduces Git and covers all the basic commands while providing some insight into what Git is and how it works. Part II includes standalone chapters on more advanced topics. These chapters are not essential to learning how to use Git and can be read as needed, depending on their relevance and your interests. Finally, the tutorial includes appendices on miscellaneous topics.

</div>

## Prerequisites {.unnumbered .unlisted}

This tutorial assumes you are using Git version 2.51.0 or newer. If you are using an older version of Git, some of the `git config` commands in @sec-configuration-of-git might not work, the `git switch` and `git restore` commands might not be available, and there might be other unforeseen issues.

This tutorial assumes that you are using a Windows machine and have Git for Windows installed. See the start of @sec-git-bash for a link to download Git for Windows. We will be using Git exclusively from the terminal with Git Bash, a Bash environment for Windows. macOS users should be able to follow along with few or no changes, since the default shell on macOS is Zsh (or Bash on older systems). Linux users should also be able to follow along, regardless of which shell they use.

As stated earlier, we will work exclusively from the terminal using Git Bash. You do not need any prior experience working from the terminal, but if you have no such experience, start by going through @sec-git-bash. 

Finally, if you want to follow along in @sec-introduction-to-github, you will need to create a GitHub account and authenticate with GitHub using the GitHub CLI, which must also be installed. See @sec-introduction-to-github for details.
